candidate.title: THS-Seq
candidate.scope: The single unbranched THS-seq (transposome hypersensitive sites sequencing) architecture in the assigned Illumina diagram, from accessible chromatin through a barcoded DNA sequencing library. The card’s engineered-Tn5 description is interpreted using Sos et al. 2016 and its Tn5059 implementation; the image itself labels the reagent generically as Tn5. The figure depicts no alternative target workflows. Its broad dsDNA-synthesis and barcode/adaptor blocks remain broad, with primary-supported material interfaces clarified.

states.label: Chromatin containing accessible genomic DNA
features: The Open DNA panel shows exposed DNA between nucleosomes. The preceding highlighted-linker cartoon is the THS-seq title illustration, not an additional transformation or a second branch.
The biological target is chromatin accessibility; the initial chemical substrate is genomic DNA in chromatin.

evidence.quote: THS-seq is a method for highly sensitive characterization of chromatin accessibility. This variation on ATAC-seq uses linear amplification of accessible DNA ends, in vitro transcription, and an engineered Tn5 super-mutant.

states.label: Tn5 transposome loaded with custom DNA transposons
features: The blue complex is the transposase reagent. Its oligonucleotide cargo carries green T7-promoter and red read-primer/adaptor sequence elements; the Read primer label denotes a sequence element in this cargo.
Primary-source transposons also contain mosaic-end sequences for Tn5 binding. Those sequences are not separately identified in the Illumina image.
The figure labels the enzyme generically as Tn5; the card’s engineered super-mutant corresponds to Tn5059 in the primary implementation. This does not identify every Tn5 reagent as equivalent.

Genomic-flank sequences in the cDNA are the sequenced readout carrier. Mapping their occurrence/enrichment to genomic positions supports a chromatin-accessibility profile and is an indirect proxy for protein-DNA interactions.
The primary discussion acknowledges background transposition. Accordingly, insertion recovery supports accessibility enrichment rather than perfect biological specificity at every recovered site.

operations.label: Insert in regions of open chromatin
operations.description: Apply the loaded Tn5 transposome to chromatin. Transposition cleaves accessible DNA and installs the custom promoter/read-primer tags at the resulting DNA ends, producing insertion-tagged chromatin DNA.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 is the catalyst within the delivered transposome reagent; transposon DNA is incorporated into the product. The primary implementation uses Tn5059 and a custom transposon containing mosaic ends, a T7 promoter and an Illumina-compatible adaptor sequence. The icon is not a separate transposome-generation operation.
operations.information_effect: Insertion positions associate introduced sequences with accessible genomic DNA. Promoter-bearing ends permit later RNA amplification of insertion-site flanks; the primary design makes usable ends without requiring a particular transposon orientation.

operations.label: Purify
operations.description: Recover insertion-tagged DNA from the post-transposition chromatin material, removing chromatin-associated proteins and transposase so that tagged DNA can enter the fill-in/IVT block.
operations.mechanism: The paper resolves the broad purification interface as protein removal followed by DNA recovery. The schematic leaves its execution details inside this block.
operations.information_effect: Retains the genomic sequences and attached promoter/adaptor elements while removing their protein association.

operations.label: End fill-in and IVT amplification
operations.description: Fill in the tagged DNA ends, then use the introduced T7 promoters to transcribe and linearly amplify insertion-adjacent genomic sequences. The product passed to the next block is RNA.
operations.mechanism: End fill-in prepares the insertion-tagged DNA template; T7 RNA polymerase then generates RNA copies from the introduced promoter. The two actions remain one local operation because the diagram groups them under one caption.
operations.information_effect: Copies the sequence information at accessible DNA ends into RNA. The primary design captures insertion-end information regardless of the distance to a neighboring insertion.

method_scopes.rationale: The card heading and left image title identify THS-seq as the sole schematic target, and the paper directly describes its promoter-tagging, linear RNA amplification and cDNA-library architecture. Every listed operation belongs to this drawn THS-seq route. The title cartoon and Open DNA panel describe the same chromatin target; the two insertion ends and parallel product lines do not establish branches. ATAC-seq comparisons and EzTn5 experiments in the paper do not add depicted targets. The paper’s embedded custom RNA-seq procedure supplies the cDNA and library-finishing interfaces within this assay. No interchangeability of enzyme implementations is asserted.
